title.narrative: Activity under preparation Global Gateway Clean Energy Investment & Climate-Resilient Transformation Support

description.narrative: This action supports the Global Gateway objective of accelerating clean energy transition and mobilising sustainable investment for priority clean energy and electricity infrastructure projects mainly in Sub-Sahara Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean (LAC) in line with Global Gateway, the EU¿s climate diplomacy and the Global Gateway Investment Hub. It is also aligned with broader Africa¿Europe cooperation frameworks, notably the Africa¿Europe Green Energy Initiative (AEGEI). The action could also cover Asia-Pacific depending on the opportunities to leverage investment in the region. In terms of geographic scope, the action will follow a subsidiary principle, meaning it will be implemented where other EU funding sources (e.g. EU Delegations) are not available, and therefore may not necessarily be active in all the regions mentioned above. It responds to persistent bottlenecks that slow investment: insufficient market rules and private sector access, lengthy and complex permitting and procurement processes, and limited transaction preparation capacity and risk allocation for bankable tenders¿combined with information asymmetries and weak matchmaking between project opportunities, private sector consortia and finance providers. It also contributes to advancing EU climate change policy objectives in partner countries. The action delivers an integrated ¿policy-to-deal¿ support offer, implemented through demand-driven assignments and service packages prioritised in coordination with Commission services and EU Delegations. It aims to (i) strengthen market, policy and regulatory frameworks (including electricity market design and procurement mechanisms) and (ii) mobilise investments in Global Gateway-aligned clean energy and electricity infrastructure projects by supporting transaction preparation, tender participation and access to finance. In this context, the action supports the efforts of the Global Gateway Investment Hub to mobilise investment. It contributes primarily to SDG 7 (Affordable and Clean Energy) and SDG 13 (Climate Action), with additional contributions to SDG 9 (Industry, Innovation and Infrastructure) and SDG 17 (Partnerships). In line with the action¿s OPSYS markers, climate is treated as a principal objective; gender equality is integrated as a significant objective through mainstreaming in assignment design, stakeholder engagement and capacity building. Three mutually reinforcing outputs will be delivered. Output 1 provides upstream support to partner-country institutions on market, policy and regulatory frameworks (including electricity market design and procurement, tender as well as auction frameworks), helping to create predictable, transparent and investable rules and processes, while improving conditions for European investment participation.
